correctness.rationale: For every integer \(r\ge3\), symmetry averaging reduces the unrestricted Dirac-commutator minimization to a single parameter. The antipodal skew block has norm \(\sqrt{r-1}\). For the adjacent orbit, the exact 5-dimensional active subspace splits into a 3-by-2 block \(C_r(a)\); its explicitly computed Gram matrix yields the stated maximum eigenvalue \(F_r(a)\). Full-column-rank derivative gives strong convexity and unique minimizer in (-1/2,0), and a diagonal Gram bound proves strict class separation. Uniform large-r expansion of the larger eigenvalue, differentiation, and binomial series establish the two gap coefficients. The packaged checker passed 219 tests; finite checks are not used as the proof for all r.

value.rationale: The cocktail-party graph is the canonical cross-polytope one-skeleton and has exactly two vertex-pair orbits. A complete spectral-metric classification for the full dimension family is a natural invariant, not an arbitrary finite slice. The exact optimizer, strict class separation, and two-term asymptotic gap \(1/(8r^{3/2})+1/(128r^{5/2})\) quantify a structural collapse of graph-geodesic lengths 1 versus 2 under the adjacency-Dirac metric; this does not follow from general upper/lower estimates.
